clue.text: Trophy item that could be unobtrusive, but possibly not needed

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters of the word unobtrusive may be remade, once 'but' is taken away from them

parts.note: these three letters are 'possibly not needed', so they come out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a trophy piece could sit quietly on the shelf, though perhaps nobody really needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: UNOBTRUSIVE holds the letters of the answer plus B, U, T; 'could be' signals the rearrangement and 'possibly not needed' says BUT is the surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake brought home from a trip or event is a memento, a trophy kept as a reminder.

clue.text: Being fanciful about mountain climbing's code of ethics?

indicators.note: 'about' means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a fairy is a fanciful being, one from fairy tales

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for mountain is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A wry question whether climbers' unwritten rules are mere fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being fanciful' looks like a verb phrase, but it is a noun: a fanciful being. 'climbing' reverses the mountain upwards in this down light, and 'about' wraps the fanciful being round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest, sporting conduct and respect for the rules is the standard of decent behaviour, a moral code.

clue.text: Lord half-cut in tartan? Maybe he can't grow up

indicators.note: 'in' places the trimmed peer inside the tartan garment

parts.note: tartan stands for the kilt, the tartan skirt of Highland dress

indicators.note: half-cut means half of the word is cut away, leaving only its first two letters

parts.note: a duke is a lord of the highest rank

explanation.surface: A tipsy aristocrat in Highland dress behaves like an overgrown child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves the peer; tartan stands for the Scottish garment made of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word blends kid and adult: a grown-up who keeps childish tastes and never matures.

clue.text: Pasquale boring? Aged brainy bits!

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so his name gives ME
boring means dull
AE is short for Latin aetatis, 'aged', as on gravestones

explanation.surface: The setter mocks himself as dull and old, then boasts of his clever bits.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often stand for ME or I; AE (aetatis, 'at the age of') is a classical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the inner parts of organs, including the medulla oblongata at the base of the brain, so playfully bits of the brain.

clue.text: Severe critic to have fresh go at racist

indicators.note: fresh means made anew, so the words go at racist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh reviewer gets ready to lay into a bigot once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who castigates scolds or reprimands severely, so a harsh fault-finder.

clue.text: One American going up in plane, a man of habit

indicators.note: 'in' places the turned pair inside the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A lone American climbs in an aircraft; the passenger is a creature of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of habit' suggests routine, but the habit is a religious garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Society of Jesus are priests in religious orders, who wear a cassock or habit.

clue.text: Philosopher recalled memory of top people

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the memory abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: A thinker remembers the elite of his day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' suggests remembering, apt beside memory, but it signals the computer memory abbreviation read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who thinks and teaches about right and wrong is a kind of ethical thinker.

clue.text: Fractions? That'll finish classes off!

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: the word classes has three letter S's

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic reading: the final letter of 'classes' is its third S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing something into three equal parts gives these fractions, each one part in three.

clue.text: Story about journalist on top of the world

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the story word is read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A tale about a reporter at the summit of Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling on top of the world is an idiom for being overjoyed, thrilled.

clue.text: See 24
Hesitating to oust leader, admitting even Boris ultimately not seen as popular?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the doubtful word holds the trimmed even word inside it
ousting the leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: being dubious is hesitating, unsure

indicators.note: 'not' says the final letter of Boris must not be there

parts.note: quits means even, all square after a debt is paid

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the name Boris

explanation.surface: A political jibe: even Boris, ousting his leader, turns out unpopular.
explanation.walkthrough: UBIOUS (DUBIOUS, its leader ousted) takes in QUIT (QUITS losing S, Boris's last letter). The definition is loose and playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everywhere is seen all over the place, as if universally popular; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Bad person, no saint, that may offer something for the writer

definitions.text: that may offer something for the writer

indicators.note: 'no saint' means the saint's abbreviation is absent

parts.note: a stinkpot is a nasty, contemptible person

explanation.surface: A rotter, no saint at all, who may yet give the writer some material.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pot holds ink for dipping a pen, offering a supply to someone writing.

clue.text: Style one noticed in remuneration? Cash now only in £50 notes

indicators.note: noticed in means seen inside, so the pieces sit within the pay word

parts.note: remuneration is pay
a perm is a permanent wave, a hair style

explanation.surface: A hair stylist gets tipped only in large notes these days.
explanation.walkthrough: '£50 notes' is cheeky: banknotes of any value are this cash, which is all that the definition needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes, as opposed to coins, are cash printed on paper; the definition jokes about high denominations.

clue.text: Agent wants Alli to attract crowd at match

parts.note: Dele Alli is an English footballer
the gate is the attendance at a sports match

explanation.surface: A footballer's agent wants him to draw big crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Dele Alli was an England midfielder; GATE is British for match attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative sent to act on behalf of others serves as their agent.

clue.text: Gone after final wish for something that's far too expensive

indicators.note: after puts the gone word behind the final wish

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the last wish on a tombstone
gone, as in food gone bad, means off

explanation.surface: Someone expires after a last request, leaving an overpriced bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or overcharge is informally called a racket or fleecing, something far too costly.

clue.text: Supporting medieval buildings permanently

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
keeps are the central towers of medieval castles

explanation.surface: Backing the preservation of castles for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means for good, forever, never to be returned.

clue.text: Give sign of respect, having received shocking treatment

indicators.note: having received means taking in, so the bow holds the treatment

parts.note: a bow is a sign of respect
EST is electroshock therapy

explanation.surface: A patient bows in gratitude after a jolting therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' suggests outrage but means electric shock: EST, electroshock treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to confer, to present as a gift.

clue.text: Little stories about Beckham's innermost character in magazines

indicators.note: about means around, so the little stories go around the central letter

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
lies are stories, fibs

indicators.note: the innermost character of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Tabloid magazines run small fibs about David Beckham's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innermost character' sounds like personality, but it is the middle letter of BECKHAM, K.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodicals published once every seven days are named for their schedule.

clue.text: Songbird not weak at heart growing bigger

indicators.note: 'not weak' means the abbreviation for weak is removed
at heart says the removed letter is the one in the middle of the bird

parts.note: the waxwing is a songbird

explanation.surface: A strong-hearted songbird putting on size.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is said to wax as it grows fuller, so waxing means increasing.

clue.text: Go wrong in atria, wrong environments for plants

indicators.note: 'in' puts the error verb inside the jumbled atria
the second wrong means the letters of atria are put wrong, scrambled

parts.note: to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: Plants in a building's atrium wrongly placed fail to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'wrong' scrambles the atria to TARIA, and the error verb goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass enclosures for growing plants or keeping small animals are vivariums, controlled habitats.

clue.text: Life of religious minister English Society's elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means lifted to the top, so these two letters move to the start

parts.note: a priest is a religious minister
E is English and S is Society

explanation.surface: A clergyman's life, his English society raised in status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' lifts ES from the end of PRIEST to the top of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for spirit means liveliness, vivacity, wit.

clue.text: Aztec leader being deposed sadly with soldiers entering — led by me?

definitions.text: Aztec leader being deposed sadly with soldiers entering — led by me?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the soldiers go into the jumbled letters
sadly signals the remaining letters are disordered
the leader of Aztec is its first letter, removed

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers

explanation.surface: The fall of the Aztec king, brought down by a conquistador's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue as definition: the Spaniard Hernán Cortés (also spelt Cortez) led the troops that deposed the Aztec ruler Montezuma.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish conqueror of Mexico led the soldiers who toppled the Aztec emperor, matching 'led by me'.

clue.text: Pledge from left-winger falling short over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the time letter
falling short means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a commie is a communist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: A promise from a socialist that falls short over time.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge is to bind oneself, to promise firmly.

clue.text: No promises to be broken? It sounds the wrong way round

definitions.text: It sounds the wrong way round

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the words no promises are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that promises exist to be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping the opening sounds of words, like Rev Spooner, makes phrases come out back to front.

clue.text: Respond to demand of traffic cop in jumper

definitions.text: Respond to demand of traffic cop
definitions.meaning: to bring a car to the roadside when a police officer signals
a jumper is a knitted sweater

explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater, not someone who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers stop at the kerb when told to, and the same phrase names a sweater pulled on over the head.

clue.text: See 2
Something a bit hairy about community we're leaving? Get better informed!

indicators.note: about means round, so the hairy bit goes round the community

parts.note: a wisp is a thin strand of hair
the EU, the European community the UK was leaving at the time

explanation.surface: A grumble about Brexit: wise up before it gets hairy!
explanation.walkthrough: Written during Brexit, so the community 'we're leaving' is the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to become aware, to learn the truth of a situation.

clue.text: Looked disgusted, given ghastly publicity about church

parts.note: ghastly means grim

indicators.note: about means around, so the publicity goes round the church

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face at lurid advertising about the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a face, twisting the features in distaste, is how disgust shows.
